# The method lab

*Generated by `scripts/methodlab.py`.*

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-SCOPE">This page holds experiments on this project's methods: what the
monitoring archive could have detected, what an estimator recovers when the truth is
stipulated in advance, and where a chain of reasoning feeds on itself. Its one statement
about the water is a bound, read from the real archive through a simulation and holding
only under that simulation's assumptions. It is kept apart from the pages that argue
about water because a reader who cannot tell which claims rest on measurement and which
on simulation is entitled to distrust both.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-SCOPE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## This is not a new method, and that matters

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OSSE">Building a known world, sampling it the way the real instrument
samples, and checking whether the analysis recovers what was put in, is an established
method. In meteorology and oceanography it is an **Observing System Simulation
Experiment**: a *nature run* stands in for the world, synthetic observations are drawn
from it with realistic error, and the analysis is scored against a truth that is known
because it was constructed. The experiment below is one in miniature.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-OSSE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-OSSE-THEIRS">OSSEs are widely used to evaluate future observing systems
and network designs ([Fujii et al., *Frontiers in Marine Science*,
2019](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/marine-science/articles/10.3389/fmars.2019.00417/full)).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-OSSE-THEIRS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-POWER">The same logic under another name is prospective power analysis -
sizing an experiment by what it could detect, before it is run - which clinical-trial
guidelines require ([the ICH guideline on statistical principles for clinical
trials](https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/ich-e-9-statistical-principles-clinical-trials-step-5_en.pdf)).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-POWER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-LICENSE">So the objection worth taking seriously is not *this method has
no precedent*. It is the narrower one: **a simulation on its own licenses claims about the
instrument, not about the world.** A claim about the world needs a measurement: the bound
below is the real archive's spread read through the simulation, and it holds only under
the simulation's assumptions. The table at the end lists instances. The build refuses a
number built on simulation on any page but a method page; prose is not checked.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-LICENSE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 1. What could this archive have seen?

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-METHOD">`scripts/detectable.py` takes the **[62,069](SOURCES.md#F-e0f0762bda) surface-oxygen
samples** the real estimate uses - read through `cycles.read_samples()`, so with the same
filters and the same clock - imposes a cycle proportional to the sine of the sun's
elevation at each sample's instant and place, adds noise measured from the archive, and
runs the estimator itself: `cycles.deviations()`, with its window and sun bins, and one
rule, applied to both sides, for which bins count. Each size is run on [40](SOURCES.md#F-6f098c6900) noise
draws, the round-the-clock comparison on fewer. It claims nothing about how the sea
behaves. It asks only: *if it behaved this way, at this size, would this schedule have
found out?*</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-METHOD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-LEFT-OUT">Left out: [18,717](SOURCES.md#F-ec36127728) samples whose clock is a filled-in default
and [10,198](SOURCES.md#F-73c5894b06) from suppliers whose clock convention is mixed. Neither can be placed
against the sun.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-LEFT-OUT "What this claim rests on")</sup> See *The clock itself* below.

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-TABLE-READ">The medians are shown; *middle of the draws* runs from about
the fifth to the ninety-fifth percentile. A loss is given only where the median recovery
clears the ninety-fifth percentile of what no cycle produces.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-TABLE-READ "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-WORKDAY">**The working day costs between [77](SOURCES.md#F-c36645eb60)% and [79](SOURCES.md#F-c74ab00bcf)% of a
sun-shaped daily cycle**, steadily across a [4](SOURCES.md#F-d56e7edf04)-fold range of sizes - every size
large enough to recover above the noise.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-WORKDAY "What this claim rests on")</sup>
<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-ASSUMPTION-FREE">The same samples, stations and seasons are compared
with themselves, only the hour redrawn, so no model of the sea's mean state or seasons
enters. What does enter is the stipulated sun-shaped cycle and Gaussian noise of the
measured size, against a round-the-clock schedule with the hour drawn uniformly; a cycle
peaking at another hour would lose a different share.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-ASSUMPTION-FREE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**The observed spread is not evidence of a cycle.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-SPREAD-NOT-EVIDENCE">The real
archive shows a spread of [0.0581](SOURCES.md#F-65d38500a4) mg/l across the sun bins. With no cycle imposed at all,
[8](SOURCES.md#F-940dbf62e4)% of draws produce one at least as large, which is too often for the
observed spread to count as a sign of one.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-SPREAD-NOT-EVIDENCE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**The bound.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-DIURNAL-BOUND">A cycle of size [0.7](SOURCES.md#F-8ebae27cb6) mg/l produces a spread
at least as large as the observed one in [100](SOURCES.md#F-c7e47f4bca)% of draws, and
every smaller size on the grid does so in fewer than [95](SOURCES.md#F-7b5eb17f56)% of them. So if
the real surface cycle follows the sine of the sun's elevation, its size is below
[0.7](SOURCES.md#F-8ebae27cb6) mg/l. The size is the coefficient on that sine: the swing from night to noon it
would give where the sun stands overhead, and more than the swing on any Danish day.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-DIURNAL-BOUND "What this claim rests on")</sup>
<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-BOUND-STRONGER">A bound is a stronger object than a null: a null cannot separate *the effect is absent* from *the instrument could not have seen it*, and a bound can.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-BOUND-STRONGER "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-NOISE-MEASURED">Noise is measured from the archive, at **[0.8427](SOURCES.md#F-1bae49478e) mg/l**,
from [11,244](SOURCES.md#F-69439f944a) samples whose window neighbours all share their sun bin, so the
contrast between bins cannot enter it; its Gaussian form is stipulated.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NOISE-MEASURED "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### What the estimator has to work with

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-NEIGHBOURS">The estimator sees a diurnal signal only through contrast
*within* a station's own ±[10](SOURCES.md#F-7bf99180a0)-day window. Of the [62,069](SOURCES.md#F-e0f0762bda) samples,
**[64](SOURCES.md#F-e7c15fb4e1)% have no other sample from their station inside that window** and
contribute nothing. Of the [22,571](SOURCES.md#F-9148e6492c) that do, **[11,244](SOURCES.md#F-8ff12c92e4) - [50](SOURCES.md#F-6a54df89ac)% - have neighbours only
in their own sun-elevation bin**, and so add no contrast between bins. Whatever this
estimator can say about the daily cycle rests on the rest.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NEIGHBOURS "What this claim rests on")</sup>

### The clock itself

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-TECH-INSTRUCTION">The technical instruction for Danish marine monitoring asks for sampling times in UTC.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-TECH-INSTRUCTION "What this claim rests on")</sup>
<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-CLOCK-KINDS">`Startklok` is not UTC wherever that can be tested, and it is
not one kind of thing. `scripts/clockzone.py` compares every station with itself in the
weeks either side of each summer-time change: a wall clock does not move, a UTC clock
jumps an hour one way, a clock with the offset added jumps the other. Until the late
nineties the archive's times are Danish wall-clock times with the offset *added*, mixed
with filled-in defaults that read noon and three in the morning local once the offset is
taken off; from the early two-thousands they are wall-clock times; and some suppliers'
conventions are mixed.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-CLOCK-KINDS "What this claim rests on")</sup>
<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-CLOCKPY">Every analysis that places a water-chemistry sample in time takes the instant from `scripts/clock.py`, which returns one UTC instant or says why there is none; the raw column is read elsewhere only for fixed readings kept as controls and a clock-hour count no page uses.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-CLOCKPY "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 2. The circularity register

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-CIRC-INTRO">Each item below is a way a check on this project's methods can
pass without testing what it seems to test. The failure is silent: a circular
check passes.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-CIRC-INTRO "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**The noise that contains the signal.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-NOISE-CIRC">The bound above depends on an estimate of
the noise the estimator must see through. Taken as the archive's within-cell
residual spread, that estimate would contain whatever diurnal signal exists, so
a large real cycle would inflate the yardstick used to rule a large real cycle
out - and a noisier null reaches the observed spread more often, so the bias
would favour this page's conclusion that the spread is not a cycle.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NOISE-CIRC "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-NOISE-NOW">The noise is
therefore taken only from samples whose window neighbours all fall in their own
sun-elevation bin, so only the diurnal variation inside one bin can enter it.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NOISE-NOW "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Comparing a simulation with an observation.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-ONE-ESTIMATOR">The two are compared
through one estimator called on both sides: the observed spread and every
synthetic recovery come from `cycles.deviations()`, with the same window, the
same sun bins and the same rule for which bins count, over [40](SOURCES.md#F-6f098c6900) noise
draws per amplitude.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-ONE-ESTIMATOR "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Validating a flow model against a flood model.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-FLOOD-MODEL">The 2012 Copenhagen
sheets are calculated flood scenarios for a hundred-year event, published by
Københavns Kommune: the output of a model, not a record of flooding. Which model,
over what terrain, and whether it included the sewers, is not stated in anything
this project holds.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-FLOOD-MODEL "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-FLOW-VS-FLOOD">Scoring a terrain-driven flow model
against them measures agreement with another model, not correctness against the
world, so they can serve as a sanity check and not as truth.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-FLOW-VS-FLOOD "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-CATCHMENT-RULE">The same will hold for
official catchment delineations when this project's own flow model is scored
against them: agreement will be a sanity check, not a validation.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-CATCHMENT-RULE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Borrowing a clock and then analysing the hour.**
<span class="claim" data-claim="C-DEPTH-BORROW">[4,688,007](SOURCES.md#F-d4ab94d60c) oxygen measurements at depth were placed in time
with a clock borrowed from a same-day water-chemistry bottle, and
[2,454,520](SOURCES.md#F-566c0ca9ca) had no bottle with a usable time to borrow from - none that day,
or one whose clock is a filled-in default or of a mixed convention. The two
counts are not shares of one population: the first is counted after
`scripts/depth_clock.py`'s quality filters and the second before them.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-DEPTH-BORROW "What this claim rests on")</sup>
<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-BORROW-ARTEFACT">If casts systematically precede bottles, any diurnal pattern found at
depth is partly an artefact of the borrowing.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-BORROW-ARTEFACT "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-DEPTHCLOCK-CHECK">`scripts/depth_clock.py` therefore
uses supplied field-sheet times where they exist and, where a cast has both a
supplied and a borrowed time, reports the distribution of the offset between
them - so supplied times check the borrowed clock as well as replacing it. Until
such times exist it reports the check as not run, instead of reporting an
unchecked number as a result.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-DEPTHCLOCK-CHECK "What this claim rests on")</sup>

**Tuning to match, then citing the match.** <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-TUNING">If a model is adjusted until it
reproduces an official product, agreement with that product stops being evidence
that the model is right. It is written down here in advance because the
temptation arrives later, at the moment a divergence appears and looks like a
mistake.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-TUNING "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 3. The noise floor of an acceptance criterion

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-DCE-SCOPE">[OBSERVING.md](OBSERVING.md) examines the statistical models DCE built
to calculate how far nutrient inputs must fall for Danish fjords and coastal
waters to reach good ecological status, at [29](SOURCES.md#F-d19671c79f) coastal monitoring stations
representing [22](SOURCES.md#F-8878751ad3) water bodies.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-DCE-SCOPE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-DCE-METHOD">DCE choose each model's variables by
stepwise, cross-validated regression on a calibration part of the data,
offering each candidate - nutrient and freshwater inputs, wind, light, salinity,
stratification, temperature - over up to [43](SOURCES.md#F-8efcb0db8f) period windows. They set the
number of variables by weighing calibration against validation performance,
evaluate the model on held-out data, refit it on all the data, and accept it on
several criteria, of which an $R^2$ of at least [0.4](SOURCES.md#F-2cf443d3cf) is one.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-DCE-METHOD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-REPLICATION">The simulation below does not run that procedure. It runs a simpler
one: an exhaustive search over every set of up to [3](SOURCES.md#F-51d2dc800e) of [8](SOURCES.md#F-9762b4db21) candidates,
[92](SOURCES.md#F-cea9326ff7) sets in all, scored by in-sample $R^2$, with no period windows,
no cross-validation and no held-out data. The two simplifications pull in opposite
directions: period windows would give noise more chances than this search does,
while cross-validated selection and a held-out check would reject much of what an
in-sample search accepts. The computation is `noise_floor()` in
`scripts/observing.py`, run [400](SOURCES.md#F-15124064c4) times per condition on pure noise:</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-REPLICATION "What this claim rests on")</sup>

| condition | median $R^2$ | 75th | 90th | share clearing $R^2$ ≥ [0.4](SOURCES.md#F-d94fbe607b) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [20](SOURCES.md#F-4cc32baa14) points, white noise | [0.34](SOURCES.md#F-cba6b62fa4) | [0.43](SOURCES.md#F-6eb2787be8) | [0.51](SOURCES.md#F-c60dff4416) | [33](SOURCES.md#F-c8a8ba7d3b)% |
| [20](SOURCES.md#F-87a783b49e) points, autocorrelated ($\varphi$ = [0.5](SOURCES.md#F-c5d1f4c257)) | [0.43](SOURCES.md#F-5f608c97c2) | [0.53](SOURCES.md#F-47975ae942) | [0.62](SOURCES.md#F-34b0abdad7) | [59](SOURCES.md#F-9178add562)% |
| [20](SOURCES.md#F-a70c80ff66) points, autocorrelated ($\varphi$ = [0.5](SOURCES.md#F-62d37089ed)), plus a shared decline of [2.0](SOURCES.md#F-2d04c4d646) SD | [0.56](SOURCES.md#F-6f2d1ea3bd) | [0.66](SOURCES.md#F-829dffeb3c) | [0.74](SOURCES.md#F-33fc6dca2a) | [82](SOURCES.md#F-77c1dbbd09)% |
| [15](SOURCES.md#F-ff3c86dc5b) points, autocorrelated ($\varphi$ = [0.5](SOURCES.md#F-18edee6b56)), plus a shared decline of [2.0](SOURCES.md#F-02bc0b7aa8) SD | [0.66](SOURCES.md#F-e5e4906951) | [0.75](SOURCES.md#F-28fbd19b06) | [0.82](SOURCES.md#F-730fbbcd3f) | [90](SOURCES.md#F-7a8d0c6406)% |

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-SERIES-DECLINE">The rows with a shared decline stipulate candidate series that are
autocorrelated and fall together over the fitting period. That is a chosen
condition, not a measured one: no candidate series has been tested for either
here, and the candidates include wind, light, salinity, stratification and
temperature as well as the nutrient inputs.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-SERIES-DECLINE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-NOISE-FLOOR">Under that condition the median
best $R^2$ from pure noise is [0.56](SOURCES.md#F-6f2d1ea3bd)–[0.66](SOURCES.md#F-e5e4906951), and [82](SOURCES.md#F-77c1dbbd09)–[90](SOURCES.md#F-7a8d0c6406)% of noise models
clear an $R^2$ of [0.4](SOURCES.md#F-d94fbe607b).</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NOISE-FLOOR "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-DCE-MEAN">DCE report a mean $R^2$ of [0.56](SOURCES.md#F-63372240e0) across their models.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-DCE-MEAN "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-NOT-FALSE">None of this shows that DCE's relations are false.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-NOT-FALSE "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-ML-R2-NO-EVIDENCE">An $R^2$ of [0.4](SOURCES.md#F-d94fbe607b) is no hurdle
for the simplified search on autocorrelated noise, which clears it more often
than not. Whether DCE's reported $R^2$ carries evidence depends on whether it was
measured on held-out data, which the report does not say; until that is known,
this is a statement about a selection procedure, not about the water.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](CLAIMS.md#C-ML-R2-NO-EVIDENCE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## 4. What a simulation may and may not license

| may | may not |
|---|---|
| *This schedule loses [79](SOURCES.md#F-c74ab00bcf)% of a signal of this shape.* | *The sea has a diurnal cycle of size X.* |
| *This estimator recovers a stipulated amplitude down to Y.* | *The estimator's output on real data is therefore correct.* |
| *This flow code conserves mass and is tile-invariant.* | *Danish catchments drain the way this code says.* |
| *A proposed survey would or would not resolve this question.* | *The question is answered.* |

The right-hand column needs measurement. That is what
[IF_YOU_HAVE_THE_DATA.md](IF_YOU_HAVE_THE_DATA.md) and
[EXPERIMENTS.md](EXPERIMENTS.md) are for, and it is why this page is
separate from them rather than folded in.
